rationale: The EyeDropper API is a near-perfect embodiment of P1: a browser tool whose sole function is to cross the page boundary and appropriate, so the only act that can paint the canvas is literally an act of theft. The Klein/Duchamp double-coding lands without wall text, and the work explicitly differentiates itself from Pure Colour (the OS picker invents) and The Blackest Black (clipboard duplicates) — this one steals. Graceful degradation in non-Chromium browsers is handled thematically ("Your browser will not let it steal"), which is restraint, not apology. G6 holds: although Klein appears in the 2026 Zone de Sensibilité work, the mechanism and argument are entirely different (immaterial receipt-burning vs. color appropriation).
reservations: The EyeDropper API's current Chromium-only availability limits reach, but the work treats that as content rather than a flaw. The "Return it" button is a symbolic gesture (the color was never actually returned to its source), which is conceptually correct but could be misread on a quick pass. Chance is purely contingent on the viewer's screen rather than any generative system, so the P5 placement is honest but thin.
revision_suggestion: Consider giving the per-visit label a more concrete provenance trace — even a coarse, RAM-only description like "sampled from the upper-left quadrant" or a timestamp of the moment of appropriation — to deepen the chance side of P5 and reward repeat visits. A small visual nod in the label to Pure Colour and The Blackest Black as sibling-but-distinct works would tighten the narrative arc.
